questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-25 update (Sky Sports July 21, Hindustan Times July 18-19, Exa search through July 25): Eight days after Andy Flower formally declined the England Test role over IPL/English-summer schedule clashes, the ECB still has made no appointment and leaked no confirmed interview shortlist. On July 19 Darren Lehmann ruled himself out (speculating the ECB already had someone in mind behind the scenes while endorsing Justin Langer), Kevin Pietersen backed Jonathan Trott on July 18, and Stuart Broad told Sky Sports on July 21 the job is 'less attractive' after Flower's rejection and he has 'no idea' who the ECB will pick (Sky cited Langer and Trott alongside Lehmann). With zero confirmed interview leaks for either Langer (who retains an IPL/LSG clash similar to Flower's) or newly available Stephen Fleming (who departed CSK July 13 and was Rob Key's 2022 choice, though he said he had not been contacted), and credible unlisted contenders active in coverage (Surrey's 3x champion Gareth Batty, England Lions' Andrew Flintoff, Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, Marcus Trescothick, Rahul Dravid), trimming top-5 concentration from 0.83 -> 0.76 (24% field residual): Langer 0.26 -> 0.23, Fleming 0.25 -> 0.23, Trott steady at 0.16, Dawson 0.09 -> 0.08, Moody 0.07 -> 0.06.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-25 FOMC preview update ahead of the July 28-29 meeting (Fortune July 25, Natixis July 24, FXStreet July 24, Bloomberg/Straits Times July 24): CME FedWatch July 29 hike odds eased from Thursday's 37.9% peak to 34.2% (65.8% hold) as Brent retreated slightly below $100 on Friday and the US paused Iran strikes overnight July 24-25. Crucially, major July 24-25 Wall Street previews converged strongly on a contested HOLD with two hawkish dissents: both TD Securities (Oscar Munoz) and JPMorgan (Michael Feroli) explicitly forecast a hold with at least two hawkish dissents led by Beth Hammack and Lorie Logan, while Natixis (July 24) singled out Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan as the clearest hike dissenter ('perhaps accompanied by Hammack and/or Kashkari') and projected Waller and Cook to join a hold alongside dovish/patient voices Williams and Jefferson (which also lowers the chance of a 12-0 unanimous hike even if Warsh pushes through a rate increase). Lifting modal twin-dissent 'Hammack, Logan' 0.21 -> 0.26, holding the April trio 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' at 0.17, raising solo 'Logan' 0.05 -> 0.07 to match trimmed solo 'Hammack' (0.08 -> 0.07), and edging the 12-0 unanimous hike down 0.07 -> 0.06 (sum = 0.63, preserving 0.37 across split majority-hike subsets, 3-4 hawkish dissent blocs including Waller/Bowman, and unanimous hold).

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-25 update incorporating July 23-24 Malaysia parliamentary breaking news (Reuters/Straits Times, Malay Mail/Bernama, Burma News International, Amnesty Malaysia, The Star): On July 23, Malaysian Deputy Foreign Minister Lukanisman Awang Sauni told the Senate that Malaysia instructed UNHCR to pause refugee registrations during rollout of its domestic DPP system AND disclosed unfinalized plans to repatriate approximately 5,000 Myanmar nationals currently in immigration detention depots by naval vessels 'subject to Myanmar's agreement / the resolution process.' While rights groups and Reuters characterize the naval-ship return as detention deportation rather than a clean voluntary refugee repatriation programme—and Rohingya returns to Rakhine remain obstructed—Putrajaya could finalize and frame a large-scale Myanmar return or companion voluntary repatriation track in August once Naypyidaw agrees, meaningfully lifting Malaysia 0.28 -> 0.36. Thailand remains the clear favorite (trimmed 0.65 -> 0.58) because Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul hosts Min Aung Hlaing in Bangkok on August 6-7 (inside the August window), Thailand hosts ~80,155 registered Myanmar border-camp refugees under an active camp-closure/voluntary-return timeline, and its UNHCR-linked border framework is the cleanest literal match to 'voluntary repatriation.' Indonesia trims 0.04 -> 0.03; Laos and Cambodia hold at 0.01 each (sum = 0.99).

questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-23 AFP / France24 reporting ahead of tonight's televised General Assembly debate (2100 GMT, broadcast by Bloomberg) confirms the exact 6-candidate field and locks in the first closed-door UNSC straw poll for July 30 (one week away). International Crisis Group UN expert Richard Gowan told AFP today: 'I find that Grossi is still the mostly frequently mentioned front-runner, but he has not locked the race up. Other candidates like Grynspan and Rodrigues-Birkett also have significant numbers of admirers.' AFP similarly singles out IAEA chief Rafael Grossi as the most repeatedly mentioned contender, nudging Grossi ahead into #1 (0.39 -> 0.43) and trimming Rebeca Grynspan slightly (0.40 -> 0.36) in a still-tight two-way lead. Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (2024-25 UNSC colleague, GRULAC woman without P5 baggage) jumps from #5 to #3 (0.03 -> 0.08) on Gowan's explicit endorsement of her broad Council appeal in an approval-style first poll. Macky Sall trims 0.09 -> 0.07 (only non-GRULAC nominee, carrying domestic repression criticism despite Senegal's endorsement), and Michelle Bachelet trims 0.06 -> 0.04 (alienated both China over Uyghur report and the US, plus Chile withdrew backing), leaving 2% residual for 6th nominee Maria Fernanda Espinosa.

local_articles.title: Ugandan diplomat Otunnu joins race to become next UN head
local_articles.snippet: inister of Ecuador; Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, a former foreign Minister of Guyana, and Macky Sall, a former president of Senegal. The selection process is expected to start in earnest this week with straw polls in the 15-nation Security Council aimed at whittling down the field. Other candidates can still join the race. Diplomats say there is no obvious frontrunner, although there has been a widespread view it is Latin America's turn to provide the U.N. leader and there has been support for a first woman in the job. Experts say the key to success will be to avoid a veto by one of the five permanent members of the Security Council, particularly China, Russia or the United States. REUTERS

questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-23 hydrologic escalation along the Danube flips the ranking sharply toward Romania and Hungary (Reuters, Libertatea/G4Media, ATV.hu, Power Trading News Europe): (1) Romania surges 0.27 -> 0.38 (new #1): Danube flow at Romania's entry plunged to 1,650-1,700 m3/s (lowest in 30 years since 1996 vs. 4,700 normal), forcing authorities to activate emergency irrigation restrictions on the Calarasi-Cernavoda stretch and execute controlled water releases from Olt and Arges reservoirs specifically to maintain minimum cooling flow for Cernavoda's two reactors; Apele Romane warned July 21 that recent rains failed to lift Danube flow, which is projected to stay near 1,700-1,750 m3/s through at least July 27, leaving Cernavoda (tight 15 cm gap between Unit 1/2 shutdown thresholds and 2003 shutdown precedent) acutely exposed. (2) Hungary climbs 0.20 -> 0.26 (new #2): BME nuclear engineering dean Attila Aszodi warned on ATV.hu (July 21) that the Danube at Paks fell 6 cm below its all-time record low (-104 cm Friday, -71 cm Tuesday), all three cooling parameters (temperature, level, flow) hit critical marks simultaneously, Paks was 'only a few cm' from a turbine shutdown and 25-30 cm from a complete plant shutdown, and 'we are not past the hardest part' (moderated slightly vs. Romania because Paks has 4 units with staged shutdown buffering). (3) Slovenia drops 0.36 -> 0.21 (#3): no mid/late-July Krsko cooling alerts, Krsko's auxiliary cooling towers held 100% power through June's heatwave, and Reuters (July 21) reported storms spreading directly into Slovenia—though single-reactor exposure keeps it a serious #3. Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 0.14 -> 0.13) faces the same record-low Danube (lowest since 1946 in Serbia) without reported cooling alerts yet; Belarus trims 0.02 -> 0.01 (sum 0.99).

questions.title: Who will top the men's javelin throw qualification standings at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The men's javelin throw competition includes a qualifying round before the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Games results for the overall men's javelin throw qualification at the 2026 Commonwealth Games Resolution Date : July 30, 2026 Accepted Answer Format : Full name of the athlete ranked first in the overall men's javelin throw qualification results
questions.current_reasoning: Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games previews on 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-23 (Hindustan Times) confirm all leading contenders—Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Neeraj Chopra, Arshad Nadeem, Anderson Peters, Rohit Yadav, and reigning world champion Keshorn Walcott—are entered for July 30 qualification, while highlighting a sharper form gap favoring Pathirage over Chopra. Pathirage (92.62m Rome DL 2026 world leader, 88.68m Doha DL beating Chopra by 3m) is repeatedly tabbed as Glasgow favourite (0.25 -> 0.28), whereas HT confirms Chopra (0.23 -> 0.20) has had no post-May meet since his 85.67m Doha return after a 9-month back/hamstring injury layoff and enters 'in the unfamiliar position of challenger' as his body continues to recover. Fit reigning Olympic/CWG champion Arshad Nadeem edges up 0.18 -> 0.19, with Anderson Peters (0.11) and 2026 world #2 Rohit Yadav (87.05m SB, 0.05) unchanged, preserving 17% residual for Keshorn Walcott, Julius Yego, and others.

local_articles.title: Chopra seeks 2nd gold, India target more medals than last edition as athletics events begin Monday
local_articles.snippet: elin top stars will be in action in Glasgow. Besides Chopra, Nadeem and Pathirage, the other competitors include reigning world champion Keshorn Walcott of Trinidad and Tobago, 2022 CWG silver winner Anderson Peters of Grenada and Julius Yego of Kenya. In the mix will be India's Rohit Yadav, who, in fact, is in the second spot among Commonwealth season leaders with his 87.05m last month. He is also a medal contender. Yashvir Singh is the third Indian in the fray. Pathirage will start as favourite for gold as he is the lone 90m-plus thrower in the world this season with his 92.62m while winning Rome Diamond League title. The 23-year-old has another three 88m-plus throws and won two DL titles this season. Nadeem, though, has been struggling for some time, and he is entering the Games with an extremely poor 78.47m effort at Luzern, Switzerland, on July 16. Peters has a season's best of 86.3

questions.title: Who will win the men's javelin throw gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled to take place in Glasgow, Scotland.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Commonwealth Games results or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the gold medallist in the 2026 men's javelin throw final. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete declared the gold medallist at the conclusion of the final. Subsequent medal reallocations will not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The gold medallist's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: First update since July 19 incorporates July 22-24 Glasgow Commonwealth Games reporting (Hindustan Times, Straits Times, Telangana Today/IANS). Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage (92.62m Rome DL, 88.68m Doha DL win) leads the 2026 world list by more than 5.5 meters over second-best thrower Rohit Yadav (87.05m) and is widely tabbed as the form favorite (0.29 -> 0.33). Meanwhile, although Neeraj Chopra is confirmed healthy and arriving in Glasgow late Friday July 24, July 22-24 reports confirm he finished 8th at 2025 Worlds, returned from a 9-month back/hamstring injury layoff with 85.67m (4th in Doha), and has had no post-May competition, entering as a 'challenger' (0.23 -> 0.19). Fit reigning Olympic (92.97m) and CWG (90.18m) champion Arshad Nadeem edges ahead of Chopra for gold in the 6-throw final (0.22 -> 0.23), with Anderson Peters (0.10) and reigning world champion Keshorn Walcott (0.05) unchanged and 10% residual for Rohit Yadav, Julius Yego, and others.
